meta.source_title: Terramechanics-based model for steering maneuver of planetary exploration rovers on loose soil (Ishigami et al.; Journal of Field Robotics 24(3), 2007)
meta.figure_or_table: Figure 11 (panel slip angle 5 deg, experiment markers)
meta.soil: lunar regolith simulant equivalent to FJS-1 (loose, dry)
meta.preparation: vessel filled with 12 cm of loose soil
meta.comparability_note: Markers found automatically (black components after morphological opening; legend excluded); each marker is the mean of one run (more than 100 samples) and error bars (1 SD) are not transcribed; overlapping repeat runs may merge into one point. Slip angle 5 deg (wheel steered relative to travel), not straight driving; slip set from 0 to 0.8 by the carriage; wheel speed 0.030 m/s. Soil is a crushed basalt lunar simulant (FJS-1 equivalent) with cohesion 0.80 kPa (Table I), not quartz dune sand, so the curve is for model checking only. Table I parameters of the same soil are in sand_parameters.csv. load_per_wheel_N derived here as 6.6 kg times 9.81.
